For a complete workflow, start with the [CPW scattering tutorial](../tutorials/scattering.qmd#configure-port-models).
This page is the detailed Driven Modal reference and links to the shared
[CPW input lesson](aedt-inputs.qmd). Driven Modal asks for a network response,
not unexcited resonant modes. Its ports use explicit integration lines. The two
ordered ports on the CPW end faces establish excitation and reported port order;
a picture of the gap cannot replace those line endpoints.
The inputs page imports M1 at a single height, which describes a zero-thickness
sheet. A Thin Film request declares the film instead: this example replaces
`layer_imports` with the 0.2 µm `NB_FILM` interval and declares that film with
a `PhysicalLayerDeclaration` whose lower face is the attachment face, so the
HFSS sheet stays at z = 0. The example writes this declaration itself; the
coupon GDS carries none.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import (
    FrequencySweepSpec, HfssDrivenSpec, HfssRunControl, LayerImport,
    LengthMeshSpec, ModalPort, prepare_handoff,
)
from scgsim.geometry import PhysicalLayerDeclaration

AEDT_VERSION = "2024.2"  # Choose explicitly: 2023.2 or 2024.2.
metal_thickness_um = 0.2
physical_layer_id = "orpen_sc_pdk:CpwFiniteGround:NB_FILM"
physical_layer = PhysicalLayerDeclaration(
    physical_layer_id=physical_layer_id,
    source_level_id="D0_TOP_M1",
    source_level_and_gds_pair={"layer": 1, "datatype": 0},
    source_interval_um=(0.0, metal_thickness_um),
    material_id="Nb",
    feature_kind="stack_film",
    physical_dimensions={"normal_thickness_um": metal_thickness_um},
    source_contact_facts={"layer_attachment_face": "lower"},
)
layer_imports = (
    LayerImport(
        1, 0, "D0_TOP_M1", 0.0, metal_thickness_um,
        physical_layer_id=physical_layer_id,
    ),
    LayerImport(201, 0, "D0_SUBSTRATE", -500.0, 0.0),
)

ports = (
    ModalPort(1, "o1", "-X", ((-250.0, 0.0, 0.0), (-250.0, 20.0, 0.0))),
    ModalPort(2, "o2", "+X", ((250.0, 0.0, 0.0), (250.0, 20.0, 0.0))),
)
spec = HfssDrivenSpec(
    aedt_version=AEDT_VERSION,
    mode="modal", gds_path=source_gds, modeling="thin_film",
    project_name="public_cpw_modal", design_name="CpwFiniteGroundModal",
    materials=materials, vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    layer_imports=layer_imports, object_bindings=object_bindings,
    physical_layers=(physical_layer,),
    ports=ports,
    run_control=HfssRunControl(
        "Setup1", "Fast20000", FrequencySweepSpec(3.0, 8.0, 20_000)
    ),
    region_padding_um=(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 1000.0),
    length_mesh=LengthMeshSpec(("D0_TOP_M1_1",), ground_objects, 10.0),
)
handoff = prepare_handoff(
    spec=spec, output_dir=Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-modal")
)
print(handoff.spec_path, handoff.script_path)
```

Endpoints and mesh length are micrometres; sweep bounds are GHz. Ports 1 and 2
retain their declared order. Choose sweep bounds and `points` for the part of
the network response you need to resolve. The example requests 20,000 points,
the default of `FrequencySweepSpec`; native setup and returned data use that
same count. The [sweep reference](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#hfss-driven-sweep-count)
provides its exact input rules. The line coordinates and bounds come from the
pinned OrPen CPW specimen. Padding is zero on its declared port sides so those
faces remain the intended ends.

Before [execution](execute.qmd), inspect the copied spec's port sides, line
orientation and source bindings. Native preparation reads back the actual
port assignments and setup; requested Python objects alone cannot establish
completion. On [strict return](returned-results.qmd), read ordered modal
S-parameters, impedance and Touchstone as this network's output. Do not call
its port ordering terminal-reference evidence or turn the export into an
unimplemented SCGSim circuit model.

Read the frequency-dependent response with its port convention and actual
controls. Keep native status and the available reported changes with it; the
[runtime reference](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#hfss-convergence-observations)
owns the raw-record and failure details.

For reference-conductor ports on the same public source, choose
[Driven Terminal](aedt-driven-terminal.qmd). The exact distinction and native
export requirements live in the [AEDT contract](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd).
